plan.title: Colon RSEM DESeq2 treated vs control DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12-sample (6 treated vs 6 control), unpaired, single-batch bulk RNA-seq colon experiment quantified with RSEM, delivered as a gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, plus a gene-symbol column) of non-integer RSEM expected counts. The per-sample genes.results files carrying effective gene lengths were not delivered, so the tximport-with-effective-length path (the consensus method for RSEM quantifications) cannot run; the matrix is used directly with DESeq2 after rounding the expected counts to integers, and this deviation is stated explicitly in the report rather than silently worked around. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median: per the knowledge base's explicit rule, it is kept through sample-structure QC (PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size/detected-gene table), inspected, and only removed with a stated reason if it proves to be a clear outlier rather than dropped by default — DESeq2's per-sample size factor already down-weights a low-depth sample appropriately. The core question ('which genes differ between treated and control') is answered with the DESeq2 Wald test (minimal pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=6 samples, median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, explicit reference level = control, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2FC, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05). Because strandedness is unknown and no alignment/BAM files were delivered (only the summarized count matrix), the strandedness-inference caveat is recorded as inherited/unverifiable rather than actioned. Downstream, the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) feeds fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (human, 2026.1, present in the reference store) followed by Reactome pathways (present in the reference store) as the second collection, per the knowledge-base rule that over-representation analysis on a short significant-gene list is underpowered and the ranked method on the full list is the default for a research question that is 'which genes differ' rather than 'test this specific gene list'. A single consolidated report step compiles QC diagnostics, DE results (with the low-depth-sample caveat and the RSEM effective-length caveat both stated), fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), and the enrichment tables with leading-edge genes and full reproducibility record.

Redundant/overlapping significant gene sets collapsed to representative sets; full table kept as supplement
Share of gene symbols that failed to map to Entrez IDs reported
If fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05 in T1S2, this is noted explicitly as the reason the ranked (not over-representation) method is the primary enrichment answer

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome, per R-0098@d01b/R-0048@500d/R-0107@976c; ranking metric dispute (R-0108@409f) resolved to 'stat' per R-0099@0a77.

caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent; a hallmark/Reactome hit is a hypothesis for follow-up, not proof of pathway engagement.
constraints: Report Hallmark and Reactome results as separate tables, each with its own collection version stated

steps.name: Consolidated DE + enrichment report with reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the full, decision-ready summary of which genes and pathways differ between treated and control colon samples, including every QC caveat (sample_01 depth, RSEM effective-length gap, strandedness unknown) and every method/version/threshold needed to reproduce the result?
steps.context: Combines outputs of T1S1 (QC), T1S2 (DESeq2 DE results, fit diagnostics), and T2S1 (fgsea Hallmark + Reactome enrichment) into one report.
acceptance_criteria: Report states: method (DESeq2 Wald + apeglm), package versions, design formula and named contrast (condition: treated vs control, reference=control), thresholds (padj<0.05, independent filtering alpha=0.05), number of genes tested after filter, number of DE genes
Report states the RSEM-effective-length caveat (genes.results absent, counts rounded) and the sample_01 low-depth caveat with the QC decision made
Report states strandedness as unknown/unverifiable given only a summarized count matrix was delivered
Report includes MA plot and dispersion plot with a one-line description of what each shows
Gene table reports unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE side by side; ranking/plots use the shrunken value
Enrichment section states gene set database name/version, ranking metric, universe, and size window for both Hallmark and Reactome; leading-edge genes listed per significant set
Reproducibility record included: session info, package versions, any random seeds used, collection versions, annotation package release

grounding.reason: Report content requirements (method/version/design/thresholds, shrunken vs unshrunken LFC, MA/dispersion plots, enrichment metadata, leading-edge genes, reproducibility record) per R-0041@059a and related report rules.
